Retrieves PDF passages, attaches citations, and abstains when the evidence is missing. Stack: Python, FastAPI, FAISS, Sentence-Transformers, Streamlit. Result: 52/75 tasks passed in the committed evaluation; 10/10 should-abstain tasks passed.

Stack: React, FastAPI, Python, MongoDB, RAG. Result: README reports 34/34 automated tests passing; approval gate before incident creation.
- [Agent Orchestration](https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/agent-orchestration.html): A task orchestration prototype that routes research and code work to specialists, reviews outputs, and records decisions in a structured trace. Stack: Python, LangGraph, Anthropic API, Tavily, Docker. Result: A documented 15.5-second example run traces five stages: planning, dispatch, tool calls, review and synthesis.
- [RxSupply AI](https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/rxsupply-ai.html): An evidence-grounded medicine supply prototype for operations teams. Validates model-selected facts against FDA records and prepares simulated replenishment plans for human review. Stack: Python, SQLite FTS5, BM25, Ollama, JSON API. Result: 10/10 regression cases passed on the retrieval and validation path; 1,600 normalized records in the dated source snapshot.
- [JobLens MCP](https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/joblens-mcp.html): An MCP server for job seekers using AI assistants. Combines official job-search API results, local resume parsing and an explainable skill-overlap score. Stack: Python, FastMCP, Adzuna API, PDF parsing. Result: Job search, local resume parsing and skill-overlap scoring run as FastMCP tools, listing matched and missing skills.
- [Lateral Movement Hunt](https://github.com/rohith-jpg/lateral-movement-hunt): A reproducible investigation exercise for analysts. Correlates authentication and execution records, then presents an evidence-linked timeline and alerts. Stack: Python, JSONL, Splunk SPL, MITRE ATT&CK, JavaScript. Result: 14 synthetic events produce 2 alerts in one scenario; includes benign controls and evidence prerequisites.
- [Workplace Systems Lab](https://github.com/rohith-jpg/workplace-systems-lab): An offline review tool for access, device inventories, SaaS seats and tickets. Produces prioritized findings and readable evidence for a systems reviewer. Stack: Python, CSV / JSON, HTML / CSS, GitHub Actions. Result: 13 findings across 6 fictional users and 6 assets; 4 automated tests pass in the local lab.

## Case studies

### RAGenius

URL: https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/ragenius.html
Type: RAG / DOCUMENT Q&A · Stack: Python, FastAPI, FAISS, Sentence-Transformers, Streamlit

Document Q&A for people who need to check the source. Retrieves PDF passages, attaches citations, and abstains when the evidence is missing.

Problem: Finding an answer in a set of PDFs is only half the task. Readers also need to know which passage supports it, and when the system does not have enough evidence.

Approach: I split documents into overlapping chunks, embed them, and retrieve candidate passages with FAISS. A FastAPI service returns the answer and evidence, while a Streamlit interface makes the workflow accessible. The answering path includes citation and abstention checks.

Limits: The same report records 42/65 document-Q&A tasks passing, with a 7.4-second average latency on that run.

What I learned: The evaluation makes the tradeoff visible: citation coverage does not guarantee a useful answer. The committed report includes short-answer and keyword-miss failures, so improving answer completeness is a clearer next step than claiming the system is solved.

Workflow: PDF documents → Chunks + embeddings → FAISS retrieval → Citation / abstain gate → Answer + evidence

Results: 52/75 tasks passed in the committed evaluation; 10/10 should-abstain tasks passed. Evaluated on a 75-task benchmark I built.
Evidence: https://github.com/rohith-jpg/RAGenius/blob/main/eval/report_v4.md

### VerticalDesk

URL: https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/verticaldesk.html
Type: FULL STACK / HUMAN APPROVAL · Stack: React, FastAPI, Python, MongoDB, RAG

An AI-assisted triage prototype for service teams: classifies a request, retrieves knowledge-base articles, drafts a cited resolution, and waits for human approval.

Problem: A service request needs a category, priority, relevant knowledge and a destination. Automatically turning a draft into an incident would skip a useful review step.

Approach: I connect a React interface to a FastAPI backend and MongoDB. The pipeline classifies impact and urgency, retrieves knowledge-base context, drafts a resolution and proposes routing. A person approves or rejects the proposal before the write occurs; an ordered agent trace records the steps.

Limits: The source repository is private; I am happy to walk through it on request.

What I learned: The boundary between a suggestion and a write matters. The project makes that boundary explicit with an approval gate, citations and a trace, rather than treating a plausible draft as a completed resolution.

Workflow: Request → Classify + retrieve → Draft + route → Human approval → Incident

Results: README reports 34/34 automated tests passing; approval gate before incident creation. Test count from the project README.
Evidence: private repository; walkthrough on request.

### Agent Orchestration

URL: https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/agent-orchestration.html
Type: LANGGRAPH / AGENT WORKFLOWS · Stack: Python, LangGraph, Anthropic API, Tavily, Docker

A task orchestration prototype that routes research and code work to specialists, reviews outputs, and records decisions in a structured trace.

Problem: A request can combine research and calculation. A single answer hides which tool ran, how the task was split, and whether a result was reviewed.

Approach: I use a LangGraph supervisor to plan and route subtasks, separate research and code specialists to execute them, and a reviewer to approve, retry or escalate. JSON traces capture the path from the original task to the final response.

Limits: Parallel execution, shared Redis state and cost tracking are next on the roadmap.

What I learned: A reviewer can be wrong when it judges new information using stale knowledge. The README documents a fix that supplies the current date and narrows rejection criteria to what the reviewer can actually assess. I would validate that change with a labeled benchmark before making an approval-rate claim.

Workflow: User task → Supervisor plan → Research / code → Reviewer → Synthesis / escalation

Results: A documented 15.5-second example run traces five stages: planning, dispatch, tool calls, review and synthesis. Example runs documented in the README.
Evidence: https://github.com/rohith-jpg/agent-orchestration#proof-it-works--real-outputs

### RxSupply AI

URL: https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/rxsupply-ai.html
Type: LOCAL AI / EVIDENCE VALIDATION · Stack: Python, SQLite FTS5, BM25, Ollama, JSON API

An evidence-grounded medicine supply prototype for operations teams. Validates model-selected facts against FDA records and prepares simulated replenishment plans for human review.

Problem: Medicine supply review involves different evidence: national notices, local stock and a purchasing budget. A generated answer can blur those boundaries or invent facts that the source never contained.

Approach: I retrieve product records with SQLite FTS5 and BM25, ask an optional local model to select facts, and independently compare every proposed field/value against retrieved evidence. Missing or invalid evidence leads to abstention. A separate planning tool works with synthetic inventory under budget and supplier constraints.

Limits: Runs as a CLI and a local JSON API. Next step: a broader evaluation that covers the optional LLM path.

What I learned: Separating model proposals from deterministic validation makes failures inspectable. Exact source agreement is useful, but it cannot establish clinical suitability or local availability. The evaluation explicitly separates the extractive baseline from the optional LLM path.

Workflow: FDA snapshot → BM25 retrieval → Local model → Python validation → Human review

Results: 10/10 regression cases passed on the retrieval and validation path; 1,600 normalized records in the dated source snapshot. Regression cases I wrote; procurement scenarios are simulated.
Evidence: https://github.com/rohith-jpg/rxsupply-ai/blob/main/docs/evaluation.json

### JobLens MCP

URL: https://rohith-jpg.github.io/projects/joblens-mcp.html
Type: MCP / DEVELOPER TOOLS · Stack: Python, FastMCP, Adzuna API, PDF parsing

An MCP server for job seekers using AI assistants. Combines official job-search API results, local resume parsing and an explainable skill-overlap score.

Problem: An assistant needs current job listings and resume context to give useful search support. That context should not require storing a job-platform password or automating a logged-in browser.

Approach: I expose job search, local resume parsing and skill matching through FastMCP. An isolated Adzuna client supplies job listings while local parsing extracts resume fields. The match score reports matched and missing skills so the result can be inspected.

Limits: Requires an Adzuna API key and a local MCP client.

What I learned: Separating the job-data adapter from the tool layer keeps a provider change from spreading through the MCP interface. An explainable score is useful for search exploration, but should not be presented as an assessment of someone's ability.

Workflow: AI assistant → MCP tools → API / local resume → Skill overlap → Ranked context

Results: Job search, local resume parsing and skill-overlap scoring run as FastMCP tools, listing matched and missing skills. Skill overlap is a transparent heuristic.
Evidence: https://github.com/rohith-jpg/joblens-mcp#features
